settings.name: innodb_io_capacity_max
settings.source: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.4 since MySQL 8.0, table of InnoDB defaults that differ from 8.0 (innodb_io_capacity_max = 2 x innodb_io_capacity = 20000), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/mysql-nutshell.html ; MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Configuring InnoDB I/O Capacity (twice innodb_io_capacity is a good starting point; it cannot be lower than innodb_io_capacity; both can be set at runtime), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-configuring-io-capacity.html ; accessed 2026-10-03. Why: raises the limit for background flushing when it falls behind, sized for the host's SSD RAID 0. Scope: server (SET PERSIST). Restart: not needed. Keep this entry before innodb_io_capacity.

settings.name: innodb_io_capacity
settings.source: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.4 since MySQL 8.0 (InnoDB default changes: innodb_io_capacity 200 -> 10000), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/mysql-nutshell.html ; MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Configuring InnoDB I/O Capacity (the default 200 suits lower-end SSDs; higher-end bus-attached SSDs can use 1000 or more; above 20000 only if lower values are not enough), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-configuring-io-capacity.html ; accessed 2026-10-03. Why: the 8.0 default flushes pages far more slowly than the SSD RAID 0 allows, which matters in the write-heavy tests. Scope: server (SET PERSIST). Restart: not needed.

settings.name: innodb_log_buffer_size
settings.source: Acumatica ERP 2018 R1 Installation Guide, Troubleshooting Performance, Step 4.2: Check the Configuration of MySQL Database Server (innodb_log_buffer_size 16M as a minimum; a larger log buffer saves disk I/O for large transactions), https://acumatica-builds.s3.amazonaws.com/builds/2018R1/PDF/AcumaticaERP_InstallationGuide.pdf pp. 84-85. This is the latest Acumatica release that publishes MySQL settings; the current help (2025 R2, 2026 R1) has no MySQL page. MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Optimizing InnoDB Redo Logging (consider a larger log buffer for transactions that change many rows; dynamic in 8.0), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/optimizing-innodb-logging.html ; 64 MiB is the MySQL 8.4 default, https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/mysql-nutshell.html ; accessed 2026-10-03. Why: invoice release and order entry write large transactions. It adds 48 MiB outside the buffer pool, so the aligned 8 GB does not change. Scope: server (SET PERSIST). Restart: not needed.

settings.name: innodb_adaptive_hash_index
settings.source: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.4 since MySQL 8.0 (InnoDB default changes: innodb_adaptive_hash_index ON -> OFF), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/mysql-nutshell.html ; MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Adaptive Hash Index (under heavy workloads such as many concurrent joins it can become a point of contention; benchmark with it on and off), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-adaptive-hash.html ; can be set with SET GLOBAL without a restart, per InnoDB Startup Options and System Variables, https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-parameters.html ; accessed 2026-10-03. Why: this is the vendor's current default, and it removes contention on the adaptive hash index latch in the multi-user tests. Scope: server (SET PERSIST). Restart: not needed.

settings.name: innodb_change_buffering
settings.source: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual, What Is New in MySQL 8.4 since MySQL 8.0 (InnoDB default changes: innodb_change_buffering all -> none), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/mysql-nutshell.html ; MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual, Change Buffer (disabling can help when the working set nearly fits in the buffer pool or tables have few secondary indexes; settable with SET GLOBAL), https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-change-buffer.html ; accessed 2026-10-03. Why: this is the vendor's current default. The 2 GB database fits in the 8 GB buffer pool, so buffering secondary-index changes only adds merge work after the cold start. Scope: server (SET PERSIST). Restart: not needed.
